title: Elastic Sprint Bands: demand-shaping, soft-freezes, and role buffers
creator: Ava Chen
description: Create a lightweight, repeatable playbook and decision simulator for mid-cycle demand shocks. The playbook (Elastic Sprint Bands) will define demand-shaping levers (defer, reduce scope, fast-track), soft-freeze thresholds, and a role-buffer matrix to preserve critical-path velocity without introducing brittle dependencies. Aim is a tested runbook + a simple spreadsheet simulator and a one-page ops card for on-call PM/ENG leads.
acceptance_criteria: One-page playbook summarizing 3 demand-shaping levers and soft-freeze rules
Spreadsheet simulator that models staffing bands, role buffers, and impact on 3 example initiatives
Runbook with RACI for triggering soft-freeze and invoking emergency tranche (who approves, who executes)
Two cross-functional reviews (Eng, Design) completed and sign-off from Head of Product
Pilot in one squad during next mid-cycle review with retrospective notes captured

decisions: Use 3 demand-shaping levers: defer (push to next cycle), de-scope (reduce acceptance), and fast-track (reassign top-role buffers)
Role buffers defined by criticality tier: Tier A (critical path, 20% buffer), Tier B (important, 10% buffer), Tier C (nice-to-have, 0-5% buffer)
Soft-freeze will be a 'soft' operational state (no new non-critical commits) triggered by objective thresholds rather than a unilateral exec call
Simulator will model the probability of meeting OKR milestones under different reallocation scenarios using a simple Monte Carlo approach in the spreadsheet

notes: Risk: If role buffers are set too conservatively, we reduce throughput and fail to deliver committed work; if too aggressive we erode team morale.
Trade-off: Prefer short, prescriptive ops card (less debate during incidents) at cost of some nuance; long-form guidance will live in Confluence.
Pilot constraint: choose squads with different maturity levels to validate the playbook across contexts (greenfield infra work vs. product-facing ingest work).
